choice: Validated the `processor` value in the URL-list import view against registered processors (falling back to the default), because it was stored unchecked and later used to build file paths, which allowed path traversal.
final:
I fixed the URL-list import so it only accepts a registered processor name. The unit and LLM tests pass (347 passed). Nothing exercises the import route, so I did not test it directly.

The weakness was in `blueprint/imports/__init__.py`. The import view took `processor` straight from `request.values` and stored it on every imported watch, with no check. Every other entry point validates it: the quick-add form, the API (via an enum and the Import endpoint's check), and the edit form.

The processor name is later used to build `{processor_name}.json` in the watch's data directory. An authenticated user (or anyone, if no password is set) could import a watch with a name like `../../x`. A later config save would then write JSON outside the watch's data directory.

I did not reproduce the traversal end to end; I traced it by reading the code. An unregistered name now falls back to the default processor instead of being rejected with an error.

CHOICE: Validated the `processor` value in the URL-list import view against registered processors (falling back to the default), because it was stored unchecked and later used to build file paths, which allowed path traversal.
